chunks.arabic_text: وَرَوَى يُونُسُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:

translations.en: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام that he said:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي الْمُسَافِرِ يَدْخُلُ أَهْلَهُ وَهُوَ جُنُبٌ قَبْلَ الزَّوَالِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ أَكَلَ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ وَلَا قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ

translations.en: Regarding a traveler who enters upon his family while he is junub before noon, and he has not eaten: he must complete his fast, and there is no make-up upon him.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «يَعْنِي إِذَا كَانَتْ جَنَابَتُهُ مِنِ احْتِلَامٍ.

translations.en: He said: "That means if his janābah was from a nocturnal emission."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a traveler who reaches home before noon while in a state of janabah and has not yet eaten. He must continue the fast and does not owe qaḍāʾ, specifically when the janabah resulted from ihtilām.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who returns home before noon in a state of janabah during Ramadan?

key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler whose fasting ruling is being discussed
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: noon, the legal cutoff point mentioned here
key_terms.صَوْمَهُ: his fast, which he must complete
key_terms.قَضَاءَ: make-up fasting required after the day, which is negated here
key_terms.احْتِلَامٍ: nocturnal emission, the specified cause of janabah in this ruling
